title: Prediabetes and type 2 diabetes screening
text: The USPSTF recommends screening for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes in nonpregnant adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity. Screening tests include fasting plasma glucose, HbA1c, or oral glucose tolerance testing. The recommendation applies to asymptomatic adults; symptoms require individual clinical evaluation.

title: Diabetes signs and symptoms
source: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
text: Possible diabetes symptoms include frequent urination, increased thirst or hunger, unintended weight loss, fatigue, blurry vision, and other symptoms. Symptoms alone do not establish a diagnosis; testing and clinical evaluation are needed.

title: Heart attack warning signs
text: Warning signs may include chest discomfort, discomfort in other upper-body areas, shortness of breath, cold sweat, nausea, or lightheadedness. The American Heart Association advises calling emergency services when heart attack warning signs occur. Local emergency numbers and protocols vary.

title: Evaluation and diagnosis of chest pain
source: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology, 2021 guideline summary
text: The guideline summary describes structured clinical decision pathways for evaluating chest pain in emergency and outpatient settings. Symptoms and risk factors should be interpreted in clinical context; this prototype does not implement those pathways.

title: Medication reconciliation prompt
source: Prototype workflow note; not a clinical guideline
text: Confirm prescription medicines, over-the-counter products, supplements, dose, frequency, allergies, and recent changes directly with the patient and clinical record. This is an information-gathering prompt, not treatment advice.

title: Cleveland heart disease dataset documentation
text: The UCI Heart Disease dataset documents clinical features and a target historically used to distinguish presence from absence of angiographic heart disease. Dataset labels, cohort, and limitations do not make a model's output a calibrated current individual risk estimate.

title: Diagnostic criteria for diabetes and prediabetes
source: American Diabetes Association, Standards of Care in Diabetes
text: Diabetes may be diagnosed by fasting plasma glucose of at least 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L), 2-hour plasma glucose of at least 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) during an oral glucose tolerance test, HbA1c of at least 6.5% (48 mmol/mol), or a random plasma glucose of at least 200 mg/dL in a patient with classic symptoms of hyperglycaemia. Without unequivocal hyperglycaemia, diagnosis requires two abnormal test results. Prediabetes is defined by fasting glucose 100-125 mg/dL, 2-hour glucose 140-199 mg/dL, or HbA1c 5.7-6.4%.

title: Blood pressure categories and hypertension management
source: 2017 ACC/AHA Guideline for High Blood Pressure in Adults
text: Blood pressure categories: normal below 120/80 mmHg; elevated 120-129 systolic and below 80 diastolic; stage 1 hypertension 130-139 systolic or 80-89 diastolic; stage 2 hypertension at least 140 systolic or at least 90 diastolic; readings above 180 and/or 120 mmHg indicate a hypertensive crisis needing prompt clinical assessment. Diagnosis should rest on the average of two or more careful readings obtained on two or more occasions, with out-of-office confirmation when possible.

title: Hypertension fact sheet
text: WHO describes hypertension as a major modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular, cerebral and renal disease. It is commonly diagnosed when systolic pressure is at least 140 mmHg and/or diastolic pressure is at least 90 mmHg on repeated measurements on different days. Lifestyle measures and, where indicated, antihypertensive medicines reduce risk.

title: Primary prevention of cardiovascular disease
source: 2019 ACC/AHA Guideline on the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease
text: The guideline emphasises team-based care, a heart-healthy lifestyle, estimation of 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk, and shared decision-making about preventive drug therapy such as statins. Low-dose aspirin is not routinely recommended for primary prevention in adults older than 70 or at increased bleeding risk, and may be considered selectively in some adults aged 40-70 at higher cardiovascular risk without increased bleeding risk.

title: Asthma diagnosis
text: Asthma diagnosis is based on a history of variable respiratory symptoms such as wheeze, shortness of breath, chest tightness and cough, together with documented variable expiratory airflow limitation, for example by spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility. Symptoms alone are not sufficient and other causes of breathlessness should be considered.

title: Stroke warning signs (F.A.S.T.)
text: Stroke warning signs include face drooping, arm weakness and speech difficulty. Time to call emergency services is critical when any of these appear, and local emergency numbers vary.

title: National Early Warning Score 2 (NEWS2)
text: NEWS2 aggregates scores for respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, supplemental oxygen, systolic blood pressure, pulse rate, level of consciousness or new confusion, and temperature. An aggregate score of 5 or 6, or a score of 3 in any single parameter, should prompt urgent review by a clinician competent in assessing acutely ill patients. A score of 7 or more is the threshold for an emergency response, including assessment by a team with critical-care competencies.

title: Sepsis-3 definitions and the qSOFA score
text: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. In adults with suspected infection, quick SOFA (qSOFA) criteria of respiratory rate of 22/min or greater, altered mentation, and systolic blood pressure of 100 mmHg or less identify patients more likely to have poor outcomes when two or more criteria are met. qSOFA is a prompt for further assessment, not a stand-alone diagnostic test for sepsis.

title: CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine equation for eGFR
source: Inker et al., N Engl J Med 2021;385:1737-1749
text: The 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine equation estimates glomerular filtration rate without a race coefficient, using serum creatinine, age, and sex. Chronic kidney disease is classified by GFR category (G1 90 or more, G2 60-89, G3a 45-59, G3b 30-44, G4 15-29, G5 below 15 mL/min/1.73m2) together with albuminuria, and requires abnormalities persisting for more than three months.

title: Metformin use in patients with reduced kidney function
source: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Safety Communication, 2016
text: FDA revised metformin labelling to base kidney-function decisions on eGFR rather than serum creatinine. Metformin is contraindicated in patients with an eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73m2. Starting metformin is not recommended when eGFR is between 30 and 45, and for patients already taking it whose eGFR falls below 45 the benefits and risks of continuing should be assessed. Kidney function should be assessed before starting and at least annually.
